what_it_does: Recommendation systems and search engines rely heavily on 'embedding tables' — giant lookup tables where each item (a product, a word, a user) is represented as a list of numbers — and training these tables requires shuffling enormous amounts of data between GPUs. High-end AI clusters use expensive proprietary high-bandwidth interconnects (like NVLink) for this, but commodity GPUs — cheaper, widely available cards — use standard PCIe slots and lack the fast GPU-to-GPU links, making the inter-GPU communication the dominant bottleneck. Frugal addresses this for commodity clusters by intelligently partitioning the embedding tables across GPUs to minimize how often a lookup on one GPU needs data from another, compressing or combining the small update messages (gradients — the corrections applied after each training step) that must cross GPU boundaries, and overlapping the communication with computation so the GPUs stay busy while data is in transit.
